dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: LAHS Green has two patents and IIT and BARC licences behind owned products (Goldust seven-day composter, patented Towgo mobile 1.5 TPD unit). Ion Exchange has decades of proprietary resin and treatment technology; Antony, EMS and Enviro Infra are mainly service/EPC operators.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: LAHS Green cites 50+ municipal and corporate clients but the deal file says much of the business comes from municipal tenders. Ion Exchange spreads across industry, municipal and consumer; EMS and Enviro Infra depend on government water contracts.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: Patents and IIT/BARC licences give LAHS Green some product protection, but composting machines face many unlisted fabricators. Antony's long-tenure municipal concessions and Ion Exchange's technology base are harder to replicate.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: LAHS Green has ₹31 Cr of revenue and 50+ clients; peers run multi-state operations, and Ion Exchange sells pan-India and overseas on ₹2,915 Cr of revenue.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: LAHS Green's FY26 revenue of ₹31.3 Cr is below every peer except Eco Recycling (₹48 Cr), and about 1% of Ion Exchange's.

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: LAHS Green is founder-run with the founder at about 95%, no institutional investor yet and FY26 unaudited. Listed peers have independent boards, audited results and exchange disclosures; Felix is SME-listed with lighter disclosure.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: LAHS Green grew revenue 25% in FY26 and projects ₹100 Cr+ in FY27 (projection not audited and stated differently across documents). Felix grew 157%; EMS revenue fell 25% in FY26.

dims.name: Order book visibility
dims.why: No order book is disclosed for LAHS Green. Ion Exchange reported a ₹2,643 Cr engineering order book at Mar 2026; Antony works on multi-year municipal concessions.

dims.name: Working-capital intensity
dims.why: Higher score = lighter working capital. LAHS Green's figure is not disclosed but the deal file flags long municipal payment cycles. EMS (297 days) and Felix (406 days) are the heaviest; Antony runs negative working capital.

matrix.why: LAHS Green is the only one in the set selling its own composting machines; most peers are EPC or service operators.
Equipment sales give LAHS Green a shorter cycle than concessions, with less recurring revenue.
LAHS Green depends on municipal tenders like Antony, EMS and Enviro Infra, but with far fewer contracts to spread the risk.
Patents and research licences are unusual for a company this size; only Ion Exchange has a deeper technology base in the set.
LAHS Green is the smallest company in the set.
Faster than every main-board peer in the set; only SME-listed Felix grew faster.
LAHS Green's FY25 audited PAT was ₹0.6 Cr; FY26 is a jump that is not yet audited.
The round's 22.2x FY26 P/E (on pre-tax profit) compares with a peer median of 16.5x on after-tax profit; 6.4x on the FY27 projection.
No listing yet; the SME route is the one Felix took.
Key-person concentration is higher than at any listed peer.

barriers.name: Patents and technology licences
barriers.note: Two patents (including the Towgo mobile unit) and IIT and BARC licences protect specific designs, but composting machines can be built around them by unlisted fabricators.

barriers.name: Municipal tender qualification
barriers.note: Past municipal references and 50+ clients help pass technical bids; turnover thresholds in larger tenders still favour bigger players like Antony and EMS.

barriers.name: Track record of working plants
barriers.note: 15–100 TPD plants in operation act as references for new buyers; the deal file gives no count of installed plants.

barriers.name: Working capital to carry municipal receivables
barriers.note: Long municipal payment cycles need balance sheet; LAHS Green's net worth was ₹6.7 Cr at Mar 2025 against peers' ₹110–1,340 Cr.

barriers.name: Regulation (SWM Rules, bulk-generator composting mandates)
barriers.note: Rules requiring bulk generators and cities to process wet waste create demand for on-site composters, but apply equally to all suppliers.

ahead: Revenue grew 25% in FY26 (₹25.0 Cr to ₹31.3 Cr, provisional), above every main-board peer here: Antony +13%, Enviro Infra +8%, Ion Exchange +7%, EMS −25%.
Owns its products: two patents and IIT and BARC licences, against peers that are mostly EPC contractors or service operators.
Net margin of 14.4% in FY26 (before tax, provisional) is above Antony (8.7%) and Ion Exchange (4.9%), though not like-for-like with after-tax margins.
behind: Smallest in the set: ₹31.3 Cr of FY26 revenue against ₹48 Cr (Eco Recycling) to ₹2,915 Cr (Ion Exchange).
Audited PAT was ₹0.6 Cr in FY25; FY26 profit of ₹4.5 Cr is provisional and before tax, and there is no FY26 audit yet.
Founder holds about 95%; listed peers have audited results and independent boards.
No disclosed order book, debtor days or borrowings, while peers report them; municipal payment cycles are long across this sector (peer debtor days 53–193).
watch: FY26 audit: whether ₹31.3 Cr revenue and ₹4.5 Cr pre-tax profit hold, and the tax-adjusted figure.
Reconciliation of FY27 revenue projections (₹75 Cr, ₹100 Cr and ₹106 Cr appear in different documents) and H1 FY27 actuals.
Order wins and an order book disclosure, especially multi-year municipal plant contracts.
Progress toward the September 2027 SME IPO; Felix (SME, ₹310 Cr market cap, 15.5x FY26 P/E) is the nearest listed reference.
valuation: At the round, the FY27E P/E is 6.4x on the company's ₹15.6 Cr projection; no verified forward estimates were available for peers.
FY26 P/E at the round is 22.2x (pre-money, pre-tax profit) against a peer median of 16.5x; P/B is 14.9x on Mar 2025 net worth against 1.1–6.7x for peers.
